$comment: Committed bibliography of the documentation section (/docs), rendered through apps/site/lib/docs-references-load.ts after a sha256 check against apps/site/data/manifest.sha256.json. One entry per work the pages cite, with the identity read on the work itself or on the project's reading note of it, and the reading level the project reached: read in full, read in part (targeted sections), abstract only, or not yet obtained. A year, a volume or an identifier is a datum of the entry, never a figure of MONARK. Two titles are not reproduced (title is null, title_note says why): each carries a word the site does not print. results holds the few statements the pages restate from a work, each with the reference, the place in the work and the statement in plain words; a formula there is the work's own. quotes holds the few passages a page prints verbatim between quotation marks, each at most twenty-five words, with the reference and the place in the work. English only, no market value, no name of a data source the project reads; the one oracle issuer named is the author of a cited work.

results.statement: Score how wrong the model was on n calibration points, take the ceiling of (n+1)(1-alpha), over n, empirical quantile of those scores as q-hat, and keep every answer whose score is at most q-hat. If the calibration points and the new point are exchangeable, the set contains the truth with probability at least 1-alpha, averaged over calibration and test points: marginal coverage.

With a taxonomy fixed in advance, predictions for the examples of each type are wrong, in the long run, with relative frequency at most the significance level of that type: validity holds per type, never for an individual case.

Without exchangeability, the same procedure still covers with probability at least 1-alpha minus a coverage gap, a term set by how far the data depart from exchangeability; the same holds for split conformal.

For an arbitrary sequence of data, with bounded scores and step sizes that never increase, the average miscoverage of the tracker after T steps stays within a stated bound of the target; with steps that decay slowly enough, the bound shrinks as T grows.

The performance of a recognition system is characterized by its error and reject tradeoff; when the reject option is exercised, some would-be correct answers are also turned into rejects, and the paper describes the optimum rejection rule for that tradeoff.

In a looped lending book, the figure a stress test flags as at risk is liquidation-eligible debt; eligible debt is not executed volume, because a position is liquidated in parts and re-buffers; and executed volume is not protocol bad debt while nothing breaks the continuous price path.
